replication.target_description: Single Japanese undergraduate study; evaluation of the author of an anti-Japan essay after mortality-salience versus control word task, moderated by measured interdependent self-construal. Supplied page 4 contains the interaction, condition main effect, and high/low-interdependence simple effects; the assigned locator does not identify one test.

n.sample_role: Participants retained in the mortality-salience and control conditions, respectively; regression model residual df=21 with five predictors is consistent with the same retained sample.
n.exclusions: Three participants (two females) excluded for equipment failure; not replaced.
n.location: Methods, Participants; Results, Table 1 and Interdependent SC and negative author rating
n.quote: Three participants (two females) were excluded from analysis due to equipment failure, with resultant 13 and 14 participants in the respective condition.

notes: The three assigned inputs have identical descriptions, study labels, and page locators. They cannot distinguish the condition-by-interdependence interaction from the condition main effect or high/low-interdependence simple effects. No statistic was assigned by audit-ID order. Replication sample and authors’ explicit narrative verdict are established; effect size and p remain null because the intended test cannot be established. The replication uses Japanese participants and continuous self-construal rather than the original European-American/Asian-American comparison, so exact target match remains unknown. Original DOI landing page inaccessible; publisher PDF returned 403; indexed CiteSeer PDF route returned non-PDF/challenge content; OpenAlex and Unpaywall supplied no open-access full text. No primary original-paper text was available for extraction.
